links.comparator_used: Conventional manual free-text supervisor investigation reports (pre-implementation, June-August 2025), without AI drafts
links.outcome: Report completeness (WHO MIM PS-aligned total completeness, primary) and narrative quality (adapted 8-domain PDQI mean, secondary), rated by blinded reviewers
links.effect: WHO total completeness 13.61 (SD 2.54) vs 11.81 (SD 3.39); cluster-adjusted mean difference 1.95 (95% CI 0.91-3.00; P<.001). Adapted PDQI mean 4.13 (SD 0.34) vs 3.61 (SD 0.52); cluster-adjusted mean difference 0.53 (95% CI 0.37-0.69; P<.001). After plain-paragraph deformatting, completeness difference 1.70 (95% CI 0.27-3.14; P=.02) and PDQI difference 0.25 (95% CI 0.06-0.43; P=.009).
links.tradeoff: Factual accuracy was not assessed and there was no draft-to-final audit, so transcription errors could propagate; accuracy rested on mandatory supervisor verification. Succinctness showed no significant gain (P=.31). Design was pre-post with voluntary, self-selected users (about 40% uptake), and the effect cannot be attributed to any single component. Several narrative-quality gains were format-dependent.
links.quote: Among voluntary early adopters, NARRATE use was associated with more complete reports and higher adapted PDQI mean scores after accounting for supervisor clustering.

design_hint: structured prompts with missing-information cues in ambient AI scribe workflow
